properties.decision: BL-68 vocabulary question 3, answered by Anthony 2026-08-01. A readiness FORECAST over time is carried as a `TemporalFact` series on the technology — "TRL 3 valid from now, TRL 7 valid from epoch 2035" — rather than as a projected `DimensionObservation` per epoch. THE DECIDING ARGUMENT IS A FIELD NAME, and it is not pedantry: `DimensionObservation.observed_at` says OBSERVED, and nobody observed anything in 2035. Recording a projection as an observation is exactly the fiction [BL-157] was filed about — a record asserting something happened that did not — and it would sit inside the very machinery a roadmap is computed from, so the fiction would propagate rather than sit still. `TemporalFact` is already defined as "a time-bounded assertion true only between two epochs", with VALID_FROM/VALID_TO and the property that any past state stays reconstructable; a readiness projection is literally that shape, so this reuses the vocabulary rather than bending a neighbouring one. TWO OBLIGATIONS THE SHAPE CARRIES, both of which must be built with it: the fact must MARK ITSELF as forecast rather than measured, because the whole value of the roadmap is that a reader can tell which epochs rest on evidence and which on projection; and it must carry CONFIDENCE THAT DECAYS WITH HORIZON, which `req:plans-move-honestly` already commits to for plans and which a ten-year TRL projection needs more than any plan does. WHAT THIS MAKES COMPUTABLE, which is BL-68's whole thesis: the epoch an increment can deliver on is the earliest epoch by which every enabling technology on its golden thread clears its stated threshold — and because the thread and the facts are both in the graph, the answer can NAME ITS REASON ("2036 because THIS component is TRL 3 today, projected 7 in 2035"), which is the legibility the row says real programs lacked.
properties.name: A readiness forecast is a TemporalFact, because a forecast is not an observation
properties.rationale: Anthony's call, 2026-08-01. Chosen over the projected DimensionObservation, which was the cheaper option and would have reused the existing per-epoch drift trail and its queries — rejected on the `observed_at` argument above. Also chosen over deferring the question until the representation ships, which would have followed this project's own recurring lesson (reproduce on real data before designing the fix); taken now instead because the forecast is not a refinement of the representation but the thing that makes the roadmap compute FORWARD rather than confirm backward, so designing the representation without it would settle the easy half against a guess about the hard one. Pairs with dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement; neither is useful alone.
